svg.text: CI/CD, from a push to two registries
One CI workflow in two stages, one publish workflow behind a gate. Nothing ships unless ci.yml's
verdict job saved a green key for the release commit's TREE (SR-WORK-RELEASE d14) -- not its sha.
FAST stage -- every push, the 2-min signal
FULL only when the ref is main
a FULL cell may skip on a verdict
only a FORK's PR runs anything.
A same-repo PR is the sha its
FAST, then FULL run WHOLE -- a
scheduled run never reads a verdict:
by hand, from the Actions tab.
re-earns a release key the cache evicted
group ci-<ref>-<event>, cancel-in-progress: true -- a newer push supersedes an older run on the same ref, main included.
⚠ A sha superseded mid-run has no completed run, so it cannot be released -- release the newer one. Nightly and push never cancel each other.
contents: read, workflow-wide; no job raises it -- a verdict is a cache entry, never a commit status.
every push · fork PRs · nightly · dispatch
2 - FAST -- linux · py3.12 · node 22 · 13 jobs in parallel · the 2-min signal (133 s on 2026-10-05, W-243 open) · never skips
shallow clone gives it zero -- silent pass
the package as a user sees it
Python and Node must rank the same
needs: [unit, e2e, build, arm] if: always() && !cancelled() && (event != push || ref == refs/heads/main) && event != pull_request
FULL waits for FAST to FINISH, whatever it concluded -- a red unit test says nothing about Windows -- but not after a newer push cancelled the run.
Why one file, not two: as two workflows a push to main started both at once, FULL took the runner slots and FAST's 2-min verdict took 6 (measured 2026-09-29).
It stays (W-243 step 4): the run is 38 jobs against the account's cap of 20, so dropping needs: brings the starvation straight back (d13).
push to main · nightly · dispatch -- never a PR, never another branch
3 - FULL -- 3 OSes · py3.12-3.14 · node 22/24 · 24 cells + 1 verdict job · the release proof · a cell SKIPS when its verdict is known
L7: Python >= 3.12 on Linux, macOS, Windows. The wheel
is pure Python -- these runners prove it.
each cell: checkout fetch-depth: 0, then full-verdict;
a hit skips every step below (W-243 step 2, d14)
e2e runs even when unit failed; Windows cells ~3x Linux
both junit -> pytest-annotate · green -> cache/save key
A green arm on ONE OS is not a green arm -- two libms disagree
in the last ulp. The OS x Node matrix is the point.
each shard: full-verdict, its third of BOTH passes, then cache/save:
or Python has no graph tier
shard 1 only -- N2, graph plane digest
harness sets FUX_GRAPH_REBUILD=1: the arm never takes Node's graph.json read (d9)
a new folder counts as code.
only a push reads; nightly and
an entry idle 7 days is evicted
verdict · save the green tree key
needs: [unit, e2e, build, arm, python, node-arm] if: (push && ref == refs/heads/main) || schedule || workflow_dispatch -- no always(): one red job and nothing is saved
ci-key.py verdict (the tree digest alone) -> $RUNNER_TEMP/ci-verdict/verdict.txt -> actions/cache/save. The ONE thing publish.yml reads (d14).
Per push to main: 13 FAST + 24 FULL cells + 1 verdict = 38 jobs, against the account's cap of 20 (d13). fail-fast: false on every matrix -- one red cell never hides another.
The release reads the verdict job's saved key, not the run's conclusion: a FULL cell green on its own saved verdict counts as green.
inputs: python (L7 floor 3.12) · node (L8 floor 22, '' = none)
Windows: TMP/TEMP -> $RUNNER_TEMP, D: not C: (W-243 step 3)
shell: bash on every step; checkout stays in the calling job.
junit XML -> one ::error:: annotation per failed test (first 20)
carries the test id + the failure's last 1500 chars to every
surface that shows a check. Called with if: failure().
Why: a session reading CI through the API sees annotations,
not logs -- and 'exit code 1' names no test.
a junit file pytest never wrote is a ::warning::, not a failure
inputs cell · python · node -> setup-python, setup-node first,
so the key sees the RESOLVED versions; outputs hit · key · path
written by Python, not bash -- Windows' D:\ temp path
cache/restore lookup-only, if: event == push; the calling
job saves the key itself, only after every step went green
pinned: checkout@v5 · setup-python@v6 · setup-node@v5 · cache/restore + cache/save@v4 · upload-artifact@v6 · download-artifact@v7 · pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1
verdict job saved the key for
ubuntu · py3.12 · permissions: contents: read, actions: read
CI must hold a green verdict for the code being released
found < 1 -> ✗ refuse. Keyed by the TREE, not the sha (d14): a FULL cell may have
skipped on an older commit's verdict; ci.yml's run on this sha is echoed, not judged.
Two strikes made it a gate: alpha.2 and alpha.3 shipped on red (d11a).
Cache entry idle 7 days -> evicted -> refused: dispatch ci.yml on main, re-run this job.
Release tag must match the package
v$tag == fux.__version__ -- else skip-existing would "publish" nothing, green
Bundle the Node read plane -- ONCE
The bundle's version is the engine's
pip install build twine -> python -m build -> twine check --strict
npm's trusted publisher names the SAME env
DIRECT, not staged: staging cost 2 releases
needs 'Allow npm publish' ticked at npmjs.com
-- set outside this repo, unassertable here
publishers are bound to the file NAME
publish.yml -- rename it and the next
6 - OUTSIDE THE PIPELINE -- named so that absence is not mistaken for coverage
Evidence, not a gate: it measures
the runner's libm, not a diff.
CI checks the ladder manifests only, in FAST
A red test on an uncommitted
